propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate wrote and maintained three Go services with unit and contract tests that ran in CI on every merge request.
propositions.rationale: The resume entry states the services and the tests that ran in the CI pipeline.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate deployed the webhook relay to a shared staging cluster and load-tested it at up to 2,000 messages per second.
propositions.rationale: The resume places the deployment and the load tests on the staging cluster and says the platform team held the release pipeline.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate released the webhook relay to production and supported it in live operation from 22 May.
propositions.rationale: The only go-live wording sits in a runbook whose pages are all marked 'Environment: sandbox' and whose go-live line names internal test tenants; the resume says the platform team held the release pipeline. The deployment rule forbids describing sandbox work as a production release or live operation when no source says it ran in production.

expectedGap: The relay's deployment is documented only on the staging cluster and in a sandbox namespace; no production release or live-operation duty is documented.
expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the Go services, the retry consumer, the instrumentation and the staging load tests as written; describe the runbook as a sandbox runbook and keep its go-live line tied to the internal test tenants.
permittedFollowUpTargets: Ask which environments the relay ran in while the candidate was at Tessera Cloud, who approved and executed any production release, and whether the candidate had run-time or on-call responsibility for it.
